title: Historic Storm Forces Unprecedented Postponement of Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
snippet: For the first time in its 100-year history, severe weather has forced officials to push the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, upending schedules and impacting major performers.
content:
NEW YORK — In an unprecedented shift for an American holiday tradition, the 100th annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed until Saturday due to severe weather threatening the East Coast. The decision marks the first time in the event's century-long history that the parade has been delayed due to weather conditions.

Safety Takes Priority Ahead of Severe Storm

Parade organizers and New York City officials announced the postponement Wednesday afternoon after the National Weather Service issued high-wind warnings alongside forecasts of heavy rainfall and coastal flooding. Wind gusts are expected to exceed safety thresholds established by the city, making flying the iconic giant character balloons far too dangerous.

"The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year's celebration," Macy's said in an official statement.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani acknowledged the disappointment and logistical challenges caused by the sudden shift, but reiterated that safety comes first. Officials noted that strict city guidelines instituted in 1998 require large balloons to remain grounded if sustained winds surpass 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph.

Schedule Upends Performers and Costs Band Hundreds of Thousands

The delay to Saturday, Nov. 28, has created major scheduling conflicts for several high-profile acts. While Broadway casts from hit shows including Wicked, Hamilton, and The Rocky Horror Show have confirmed they will perform on Saturday, others cannot make the new date.

The University of Alabama announced that its famed Million Dollar Band will have to forego the parade entirely and return home to perform at a scheduled Crimson Tide football game. The unexpected cancellation and travel restructuring could cost the band program more than $700,000 in non-refundable travel, lodging, and logistical expenses.

How to Watch the Rescheduled Parade

The parade is now scheduled to step off at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday. NBC and Peacock will broadcast the event live at 8:30 a.m. in the Eastern, Central, and Mountain time zones, and at 7:30 a.m. Pacific, with a Spanish-language simulcast airing on Telemundo.
